messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Requirement: I want to try a four-motor cluster, nothing above a D. Design a rocket that goes about 750 feet. Every section needs to land under 6 m/s.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Four-motor cluster (fixed count). No motor above a D (maximum class). Apogee about 750 ft, within 5%. 750 * 0.3048 = 229 m. Every section lands under 6 m/s (maximum). This is one stage, so that is the single section. Wind and rail not stated: 2 m/s, 1.5 m vertical rail, sea level.

2. Feasibility: Four D motors would be far too much impulse for 229 m. Four C motors may still be high once they are in the fat tube a cluster needs. Four B motors are about one D of total impulse, which is the right neighborhood. Drag-free speed for 229 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 229) = 67 m/s. Checking B and C cluster candidates.

2. Feasibility: A B6 is 4.3 N*s and 5.2 N, 18 mm, mass 0.016 kg, and the only delay is 0 s. Four of them are 4.3 * 4 = 17.2 N*s and 5.2 * 4 = 20.8 N, still a B-class motor, under the D ceiling. Four C6s would be about twice that and would sail past 229 m. Four A8s are only 2.2 N*s each and would likely fall short in the fat tube a cluster requires. The B6s fly plugged, chute at apogee, because a 0 s delay would open at burnout.

3. Size: A 4-motor cluster of 19.5 mm mounts needs about 47 mm of inside width, so the tube is 56 mm. Liftoff guess 0.14 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 20.8 / (0.14 * 9.81) = 15.1. Weight is 0.14 * 9.81 = 1.37 N, rail acceleration (20.8 - 1.37) / 0.14 = 139 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 139 * 1.5) = 20.4 m/s. A 0.45 m chute covers a burnout mass near 0.12 kg at under 6 m/s.

4. Draft: 56 mm cardboard, 0.40 m long, ogive nose, four balsa fins, one mount with cluster_count 4, four Estes B6 motors, one 0.45 m chute at apogee. Default rail and 2 m/s wind.

4. Check: The simulator gives 188.8 m. About 229 m allows 5%, and (229 - 188.8) / 229 = 18% low. Margin is 0.97 cal, under 1.0, and the burn minimum is the same 0.97 cal. Landing is 4.9 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit is 23.9 m/s, thrust-to-weight 9.9. Total impulse is 17.2 N*s, four B motors, inside the D ceiling. Liftoff mass is 0.214 kg, heavier than my 0.14 kg guess, which is part of why the altitude is short.

5. Fix: The failing values are apogee 188.8 m and margin 0.97 cal. The margin is a gate, so that comes first. One change: larger fins, span 0.075 m and root 0.11 m. I know that adds drag and the altitude may fall further. The motor stays a B cluster until the rocket is stable.

4. Check: Margin is fixed at 1.11 cal, and the burn minimum is 1.11 cal. Landing is 5.0 m/s, rail exit 23.5 m/s, thrust-to-weight 9.7. Apogee went the wrong way with the fins: the simulator gives 179.2 m, and (229 - 179.2) / 229 = 22% under about 229 m.

5. Fix: The failing value is apogee 179.2 m. The B cluster does not have the impulse, and the rocket is now stable, so the motor can step up without dropping through 1.0 cal. One change: four C6-5 motors instead of four B6s. A C6 is 8.8 N*s, so the cluster roughly doubles 17.2 N*s while staying under a D. Fins, tube and the 0.45 m chute stay. Deployment stays at apogee so the 5 s delay does not open the canopy early.

4. Check: The C6 cluster overshot, and the heavier motors pulled the margin back under the gate. The simulator gives 364.4 m, (364.4 - 229) / 229 = 59% above about 229 m. Margin is 0.76 cal at rail exit and through the burn, under 1.0. Landing 5.1 m/s, rail exit 23.0 m/s and thrust-to-weight 7.9 still pass. Impulse is 35.2 N*s, four C motors, still under a D.

5. Fix: Failing values are apogee 364.4 m and margin 0.76 cal. Both come from fins that are too small for a heavier aft cluster: not enough CP, and not enough drag. One change: span to 0.12 m and root to 0.15 m. Motors stay four C6-5s, because four B6s could not reach 229 m even with smaller fins. Tube and chute stay.

4. Check: Larger fins did not fix either miss. The simulator gives 312.6 m, still (312.6 - 229) / 229 = 36% above about 229 m. Margin is 0.75 cal, slightly worse than the 0.76 cal before the fin growth, so the extra balsa mass cancelled the CP move. Landing is 5.2 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit is 22.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 7.5. Impulse is 35.2 N*s across four C motors.

5. Fix: both failures remain. Apogee 312.6 m is still over the band, and margin 0.75 cal is still under 1.0. This was the third revision. More fin area just added tail weight. I am stopping rather than guessing at a nose weight that would have to fix the margin without being heavy enough to throw away the altitude I still have too much of.

6. Uncertainty: The cluster is Mach 0.29, so drag is not the wild supersonic kind, but fin mass versus fin area is clearly not what I assumed. Liftoff mass is 0.261 kg. A lighter fin material might have raised the margin without the altitude drop I wanted, or the reverse. Chute Cd is 0.8. Four C6 motors are also a lot of aft mass in a 56 mm tube, which is why the margin is stubborn.
messages.content:
Four Estes C6-5 motors in a 56 mm cardboard cluster rocket, four balsa fins, 0.45 m chute at apogee.
Apogee still exceeds about 750 ft: the simulator gives 312.6 m. Margin still fails at 0.75 cal.
Landing is 5.2 m/s, under 6 m/s, and rail exit is 22.7 m/s. The cluster is under a D.
